description:
The acs pipeline is hook-gated: every skill's pre-gate refuses to run until its upstream step has. This is the SPINE — the ordering every release depends on, independent of what v0.4.10 changed. Each of the 12 gated skills is driven through three workspace states, and the assertion is on the gate's exit code and the reason it gives, because the reason is what tells an operator (or a coordinator) which step to run next.

Profiles: bare = a fresh repo with settings and no tickets; ticketed = one open task ticket (TKT-1, small/low, needs_design false); epic = one open epic (TKT-1, large/high, needs_design true).

cases.title: ticketed: /code opens on the run's subject when there is no plan, with the ship.yaml advisory
cases.note: Re-recorded for v0.5.0, and the only refusal in this family that becomes a pass. Legitimate only because the BEHAVIOUR changed under REDESIGN-IMPLEMENTATION-PIPELINE.md:752-756 (every upstream artifact has a fallback chain that ends at the subject), :761 (the plan falls back to an implicit plan /acs:code derives from its own read-only survey) and :770-771 (standalone, the same missing read is the fallback doing its job). Emitter: acs_lib/gates.py:342-346. The standard/complex refusal :761 describes lives in /acs:code's own survey, not in this CLI surface, so no deterministic companion case replaces it; the case instead asserts MORE than it did — the fallback line, the advisory line (ADR-0096's cursor form, acs_lib/advisory.py:32-37) and the stdout subset.

stderr_contains: acs: no plan for this run; /acs:code will work from the run's subject instead.
acs: code normally follows create-test-docs in ship.yaml; the cursor for TKT-1 is analyze-requirements

cases.title: ticketed: /docs-sync opens out of order, with the ship.yaml advisory on stderr
cases.note: Re-recorded for v0.5.0. Predecessor: ship.yaml is a LIST and the list IS the order (ADR-0096), with run-e2e-tests immediately before docs-sync (src/acs/workflows/ship.yaml:36-37). The version-2 line named the step's unsatisfied `needs:`; there are none now — the list IS the order — so render_advisory names the run's cursor instead (acs_lib/advisory.py:11-15, :32-37). `needs:` is an authorised removal: REDESIGN-IMPLEMENTATION-PIPELINE.md §6 (:1168-1173, :1246), and ship.yaml v3 rejects it.

cases.title: epic: /create-pr is blocked — epics are never opened as one pull request directly
cases.note: Re-recorded for v0.5.0, and the EXPLICIT resolution of the GATE-042/GATE-044 contradiction, in GATE-042's favour. ADR-0101 (Consequences) records it: create-pr is in _EPIC_VERBS and GATE-042 — byte-unchanged here — requires the query to SEE that brake, so one mechanism cannot point both ways and making 042 pass necessarily makes 044 exit 2. Table: acs_lib/brakes.py:121-130 ("create-pr": "opened as one pull request" at :129), applied to every step in it at acs_lib/gates.py:352-353. Pinned durably by tests/acs/test_epic_brake_covers_create_pr.py, so the two goldens can never silently disagree again.
